proposed_comments.title: Reject unusable inspector ports

confidence.rationale: The parser directly accepts these invalid values, while TCP ports are limited to 1-65535 and the host cannot discover a dynamically assigned port 0.

proposed_comments.title: Fail closed when an entry-point segment disappears

confidence.rationale: The catch is reached only when attribute verification loses the path; treating that state as non-reparse explicitly bypasses the containment safety check.

proposed_comments.title: Report an exhausted stderr budget at the exact limit
proposed_comments.body:
### Report an exhausted stderr budget at the exact limit

**Severity:** `medium`

`_budgetNoticeEmitted` is set only when a later line is suppressed, so the property remains false when the final emitted line reaches the cap exactly. Consumers therefore receive stale budget state at EOF. Derive the status from the byte count and cover the exact-limit case.

```suggestion
    public bool BudgetExhausted => _totalLoggedBytes >= _maxTotalBytes;
```

confidence.rationale: The existing state transition is visibly delayed until another line arrives; the byte counter already represents the documented cap.

proposed_comments.title: Treat carriage returns as stderr record terminators
proposed_comments.body:
### Treat carriage returns as stderr record terminators

**Severity:** `medium`

Progress-style stderr commonly uses bare carriage returns. The current branch discards them, concatenating records such as `first\rsecond\r` and distorting both truncation and rate accounting. Emit and reset at `\r`; a following `\n` in CRLF input only produces an ignored empty record.

```suggestion
            EmitLine();
            ResetLine();
```

confidence.rationale: The current branch demonstrably discards the delimiter, and the bounded reader already ignores blank records produced by CRLF.

proposed_comments.title: Do not enable single-reader channel optimizations
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not enable single-reader channel optimizations

**Severity:** `high`

`EnqueueNotification` reads from the channel when it is full, so producer threads and the consumer can call `TryRead` concurrently. Declaring `SingleReader = true` violates the channel contract and permits unsafe single-reader optimizations. Mark the bounded channel as multi-reader.

```suggestion
            SingleReader = false,
```

confidence.rationale: Both the producer overflow path and consumer loop read the same channel, directly contradicting the configured single-reader guarantee.

proposed_comments.title: Serialize side-effecting RPC registration

confidence.rationale: The documented GetOrAdd factory semantics allow duplicate invocation, and AddRpcMethodTarget mutates StreamJsonRpc registration state.

proposed_comments.title: Retry notification admission after a consumer race

confidence.rationale: The interleaving between TryWrite and TryRead is valid and leads directly to an uncounted dropped notification.

proposed_comments.title: Isolate disconnect event subscribers

confidence.rationale: Multicast delegate invocation stops at the first exception, and this teardown path has multiple independent consumers.

proposed_comments.title: Bound concurrent inbound request work
proposed_comments.body:
### Bound concurrent inbound request work

**Severity:** `high`

Each inbound request can start another handler with no admission limit, so an extension can accumulate arbitrary concurrent work and exhaust memory or thread-pool capacity. Add a connection-owned concurrency gate around request-handler dispatch, return `JsonRpcError.ServerBusy` when all slots are occupied, release the slot in `finally`, and cover rejection after the configured limit. This requires coordinated state, dispatch, and test changes, so it is intentionally explanatory rather than a partial apply block.

confidence.rationale: The dispatch path starts handlers independently with no existing semaphore, queue, or other bounded admission mechanism.

proposed_comments.title: Use NativeAOT-safe local target registration
proposed_comments.body:
### Use NativeAOT-safe local target registration

**Severity:** `high`

`Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels` imports the repository AOT-compatibility props, but this registration discovers the target with `MethodInfo` and `AddLocalRpcMethod`. The pinned StreamJsonRpc 2.21.69 package does not expose the generated `RpcTargetMetadata` path needed to preserve dispatch metadata under trimming. Coordinate a StreamJsonRpc upgrade and register the local target with generated NativeAOT-safe metadata; include an AOT publish smoke test that invokes one inbound handler.

confidence.rationale: The project explicitly opts into AOT compatibility, the changed code uses reflection-based target discovery, and the pinned assembly lacks RpcTargetMetadata.

proposed_comments.title: Use the NativeAOT-safe named-argument invocation path
proposed_comments.body:
### Use the NativeAOT-safe named-argument invocation path

**Severity:** `high`

The parameter object is wrapped in `object[]` and sent through the reflection-oriented `InvokeCoreAsync` overload. Source-generated JSON metadata does not preserve StreamJsonRpc's argument binder, so a trimmed CmdPal build can fail outbound parameter-object requests. As part of the coordinated package upgrade, use the `NamedArgs` overload and exercise one outbound named-parameter request in the AOT smoke test.

confidence.rationale: The call directly selects the untyped object-array binder path, while the pinned StreamJsonRpc version lacks the NamedArgs API intended for NativeAOT parameter-object invocation.
